translation: The Yin Qiao is the bie (divergent) vessel of Foot Shaoyin; its vessel arises in the middle of the heel, at [the place] after the Rangu point (KI2) of Foot Shaoyin (Rangu is in the depression one cun below and in front of the inner ankle); together with Foot Shaoyin it follows down the inner ankle to the Zhaohai point (KI6) (five fen below the inner ankle); ascending two cun above the inner ankle, it takes Jiaoxin as its xi (cleft) point (Jiaoxin is on the bone above the inner ankle, between Shaoyin in front and Taiyin behind, among the sinew and bone). Ascending straight it follows the inner thigh and enters the genitals, ascends following the interior of the chest into the supraclavicular fossa, ascends out in front of Renying (ST9), reaches the throat, intersecting and penetrating the Chong meridian, enters the inner border of the cheek (qiu), runs upward and belongs to (connects to) the inner canthus of the eye, gathering with the five vessels — hand-foot Taiyang, Foot Yangming, and the Yang Qiao — at Jingming (BL1), and ascends. (Jingming is in the hollow one fen outside the inner canthus of the eye.) In all there are eight points.
